title: Two-band data set a conditional minimum column for one dip of TIC 300651846
abstract: We apply a sharp absorption moment bound to one measured CPV dip. For an opacity proportional to wavelength to the power -1 at nominal wavelengths 0.788 and 2.09 micrometers, arbitrary nonnegative column mixtures need a brightness-weighted infrared optical depth of at least 0.06469. A partial uniform column attains the bound. Conservative 95% lower bounds are 0.05127 for independent Gaussian depth errors and 0.04977 for unknown covariance with Gaussian marginal errors. An independent linear program agrees. Positive exact-depth screens show that the upper column remains unbounded. We state the additional surface brightness, radius and opacity assumptions needed to convert the column floor to mass. The mathematics has a prior absorption-doublet counterpart; this work supplies the CPV application, certificates and joint-error bounds. One selected dip, nominal broad-band wavelengths, common stellar color, pure extinction and published depth errors limit the inference. No dust mass, material life or supply rate is measured. Original code, results, a figure and fixed-source retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Minimum brightness-weighted infrared column under five assumed opacity indices, with conservative joint-error bounds. The index-1 support is below the cost at every nonnegative column.
